chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdullah al-Barqi, from Abu Talib, from Misma'a, who said:

I complained to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the harm I experienced from the food when I ate it. He said: 'Did you not say Bismillah?' I said: 'I do say it, and it still harms me.' He said to me: 'When you interrupt the saying of Bismillah by talking, then you return to the food, do you say Bismillah?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'So from here it harms you. If you had said Bismillah when you returned to the food, it would not have harmed you.'

key_terms.التَّسْمِيَة: Saying Bismillah (naming God before an action)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting Bismillah if you stop to talk while eating?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the spiritual protection of Bismillah is compromised not merely by the act of speaking, but by the interruption of the initial invocation's continuity. He instructs that one must renew the recitation upon returning to the meal, a nuance highlighted by the Imam’s follow-up question confirming the narrator's habit of speaking, thereby linking the physical harm to the lapse in mindful remembrance. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of dhikr as a safeguard against unseen harms during daily acts like eating.
